questions.q: What is a force? Describe its effects and the difference between contact and non-contact forces.
answer: A force is a push or a pull on an object, arising from an interaction between objects and measured in newtons.

answer.text: A force can start or stop the motion of an object, change its speed or direction, and change its shape. When forces on an object are balanced, its motion does not change; only an unbalanced, or net, force changes its state of motion.
These act only when objects touch — for example muscular force applied by our muscles, and friction between surfaces in contact.
These act at a distance — gravitational force, which pulls objects towards the Earth and gives them weight, magnetic force and electrostatic force.

questions.q: What is pressure, and how do liquids, gases and the atmosphere exert it?

answer.text: Pressure is the force acting on a unit area, found by dividing the force by the area, and measured in pascals. For the same force, a smaller area gives greater pressure, which is why knives and nails are sharp, while broad straps and a camel's wide feet spread force to reduce pressure.
Liquids and gases exert pressure on the walls of their container, and this pressure increases with depth.

The air around us has weight and exerts atmospheric pressure. It is very large, but we do not feel crushed because the pressure inside our bodies balances it. Straws and suction cups work because of atmospheric pressure.
